title: Galaxy Cluster Cosmology vs CMB Cosmology
bottleneck: Cluster counts via the Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect (Planck, ACT, SPT) have historically preferred lower sigma-8 than the primary CMB, though the tension has eased with better mass calibration. Hydrostatic mass bias — the offset between X-ray-derived and true cluster masses — remains uncertain at the 10-20% level, dominating the error budget. Selection effects in cluster surveys couple to cosmology in ways that are hard to model, adding another layer of systematic uncertainty.
why_it_blocks: Clusters are cosmology's most massive laboratories; their mass scale uncertainty caps their power as dark energy probes.
current_state: Weak-lensing mass calibrations from DES and HSC are improving the situation; eROSITA's cluster sample adds an independent count. Next-generation SZ surveys with lensing-calibrated masses should make clusters competitive with other dark energy probes.
